Apply a procedure to all elements of a list.

Usage: lmapcar [-concat] <object> <object>

    option              description

    -concat             concat the results into the final list

    argument            description

     <object>            name of the procedure to apply
     <object>            apply the procedure to the elements of this list

COMMAND: nl_add_net_route

Add a route to the specified net.  The default route type is ROUTED.

Usage: nl_add_net_route [-type <string>] <inet> <object>

    option              description

    -type <string>      the type of the route: ROUTED (default), FIXED, or COVER.

    argument            description

     <inet>              add the route to this net
     <object>            route to add

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_add_row_site

Add a row site to the specified design.

Usage: nl_add_row_site <string> <string> <integer> <integer> <string> <integer> <integer> <integer> [<pdesign>]

    argument            description

     <string>            the name of the row
     <string>            the name of the core site
     <integer>           the x coordinate of the lower left corner of the row
     <integer>           the y coordinate of the lower left corner of the row
     <string>            the orientation of the row
     <integer>           the number of sites in the row
     <integer>           the width of the sites
     <integer>           the height of the sites
     <pdesign>           add the row site to this design

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_compute_objective_and_gradient



Usage: nl_compute_objective_and_gradient [-delta <double>] [-wire_weight <double>] [-overlap_weight <double>] [-boundary_weight <double>] [-row_weight <double>] [-distribution_weight <double>] [-constant_weight <double>] [-cell_bloat <double>] [<pdesign>]

    option              description

    -delta <double>     compute a numeric gradient and use this as the delta
    -wire_weight <double>weight for wire length objective
    -overlap_weight <double>weight for overlap objective
    -boundary_weight <double>weight for boundary objective
    -row_weight <double>weight for row objective
    -distribution_weight <double>weight for distribution objective
    -constant_weight <double>weight for constant force objective
    -cell_bloat <double>cell bloat factor (1.0 == no cell bloat)

    argument            description

     <pdesign>           do it for this design

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_find_attributes

Return the list of attributes whose name matches the specified pattern.
By default the pattern is matched according to the rules of string_match,
which allows wildcards like '*', '?', and '[]'.

Usage: nl_find_attributes [-exact] [-regexp] [-recursive] <string> [<design>]

    option              description

    -exact              the pattern is the name of the attribute (i.e. no wildcards allowed), with -regexp this option means the pattern must match the entire name
    -regexp             the pattern is a TCL regular expression
    -recursive          find the attributes anywhere in the hierarchy

    argument            description

     <string>            pattern to match
     <design>            design in which to find the attributes

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_foreach_design_cell

Loop over all the cells in the specified design.

Usage: nl_foreach_design_cell [-hierarchy] [-library] [-unlinked] [-recursive] [-noassign] [-from <idesign>] <string> <design> <object>

    option              description

    -hierarchy          loop over only hierarchy cells
    -library            loop over only instances of library cells
    -unlinked           loop over only unlinked cells
    -recursive          recursively loop over all cells in the hierarchy
    -noassign           don't include assignment buffers
    -from <idesign>     start at this point in the hierarchy, requires -recursive

    argument            description

     <string>            name of variable to which cells are bound
     <design>            loop over the cells in this design
     <object>            loop body

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_foreach_design_net

Loop over all the nets in the specified design.

Usage: nl_foreach_design_net [-hierarchy] [-recursive] [-noassign] [-noconstant] [-noempty] [-onlyconstant] <string> <design> <object>

    option              description

    -hierarchy          loop over all unique hierarchial nets
    -recursive          same as -hierarchy
    -noassign           treat nets connected by assignment buffers as equivalent
    -noconstant         do not loop over constant nets
    -noempty            do not loop over nets that have no pins
    -onlyconstant       loop over only constant nets

    argument            description

     <string>            name of variable to which nets are bound
     <design>            loop over the nets in this design
     <object>            loop body

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_foreach_design_port

Loop over all the ports in the specified design.

Usage: nl_foreach_design_port [-inputs] [-outputs] [-inouts] <string> <design> <object>

    option              description

    -inputs             loop over the input ports
    -outputs            list the output ports
    -inouts             list the inout ports

    argument            description

     <string>            name of variable to which to bind ports
     <design>            loop over the ports of this design
     <object>            loop body

************************************************************************

Create a type with the specified parameters.

Usage: nl_get_array_type <integer> <integer> <type>

    argument            description

     <integer>           left bound of the array
     <integer>           right bound of the array
     <type>              the type of the array members

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_get_bus_members

Return a list of the members of the specified bus.
By default, the members are ordered from LSB to MSB
(i.e. the 0th element is the LSB).

Usage: nl_get_bus_members [-reverse] <bus>

    option              description

    -reverse            return the members in the order MSB to LSB

    argument            description

     <bus>               get the members of this bus

************************************************************************

    -fanios             return only the inout pins connected to the net
    -hierarchy          cross hierarchy boundaries
    -recursive          same as -hierarchy

    argument            description

     <inet>              get the pins connected to this net

COMMAND: nl_link

Link the specified design.  All cells will be linked to the appropriate
subdesign or library cell.

Usage: nl_link [-nohierarchy] [-silent] [-libraries <object>] [<design>]

    option              description

    -nohierarchy        don't recursively link all subdesigns
    -silent             don't print messages about unresolved references
    -libraries <object> list of libraries to search

    argument            description

     <design>            design to link

************************************************************************

    -libraries <object> list of libraries to search

COMMAND: nl_list_cells

Return a list of all the cells in the specified design.
By default, all cells in the current design are listed.

Usage: nl_list_cells [-hierarchy] [-library] [-unlinked] [-recursive] [-noassign] [-from <idesign>] [<design>]

    option              description

    -hierarchy          list only hierarchy cells
    -library            list only instances of library cells
    -unlinked           list only unlinked cells
    -recursive          recursively list all cells in the hierarchy
    -noassign           don't include assignment buffers
    -from <idesign>     start at this point in the hierarchy, requires -recursive

    argument            description

     <design>            list the cells for this design

    option              description

COMMAND: nl_place_design

Place the specified design.

Usage: nl_place_design [-randomly] [-wire_weight <double>] [-overlap_weight <double>] [-boundary_weight <double>] [-row_weight <double>] [-distribution_weight <double>] [-constant_weight <double>] [-iterations <integer>] [-displacement_limit <double>] [-cell_bloat <double>] [<pdesign>]

    option              description

    -randomly           place the cells randomly
    -wire_weight <double>weight for wire length objective
    -overlap_weight <double>weight for overlap objective
    -boundary_weight <double>weight for boundary objective
    -row_weight <double>weight for row objective
    -distribution_weight <double>weight for distribution objective
    -constant_weight <double>weight for constant force objective
    -iterations <integer>iteration limit
    -displacement_limit <double>displacement limit for terminating optimizer
    -cell_bloat <double>cell bloat factor (1.0 == no cell bloat)

    argument            description

     <pdesign>           place this design

    option              description

    -offset <object>    location offset in the form: {dx dy}
    -translate <string> orientation translation (N, S, E, W, FN, FS, FW, or FW)
    -filler <object>    list of filler cell types
    -zero <object>      list of logic 0 nets
    -one <object>       list of logic 1 nets
    -nohierarchy        read a flat DEF

    argument            description

     <file>              .def file to read
     <icell>             top level cell of the design to be read

COMMAND: nl_ungroup

Ungroup the specified cell.  The cell must be linked.  All the contents
of the linked design are moved into the design containing the cell.  The
cell is removed.

Usage: nl_ungroup [-all] [-recursive] [-silent] [-prefix <string>] [<cell>]

    option              description

    -all                ungroup all cells in the current design
    -recursive          recursively ungroup the cell
    -silent             don't print the name of each cell as it is ungrouped
    -prefix <string>    use this as the prefix when creating new cell and net names

    argument            description

     <cell>              cell to ungroup

COMMAND: nl_write_def

Write out the physical information for the specified design as a .def file

Usage: nl_write_def [-header] [-components] [-pins] [-specialnets] [-net_routes] [-net_connectivity] [-nohistory] [-special_only <object>] [-sort] [-zero_name <string>] [-one_name <string>] [-nohierarchy] [-fixed_only] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -header             write out header information
    -components         write out the placement of cells
    -pins               write out the placement and geometry of ports
    -specialnets        write out the special nets
    -net_routes         write out routing of nets
    -net_connectivity   write out connectivity
    -nohistory          don't write out the history strings
    -special_only <object>place the specified nets in the specialnets section only
    -sort               sort nets, pins, and components before writing them out
    -zero_name <string> name of logic zero net (e.g. GND)
    -one_name <string>  name of logic one net (e.g. VDD)
    -nohierarchy        write out DEF for one level of hierarchy only
    -fixed_only         only include components with fixed placement

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the .def file to write
     <design>            design to be written

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_pdef

Write out the physical information for the specified design as a .pdef file

Usage: nl_write_pdef [-fixed_only] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -fixed_only         only include components with fixed placement

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the .pdef file to write
     <design>            design to be written

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_sim

Write a .sim representation of the specified design to a file.

Usage: nl_write_sim [-hierarchy] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -hierarchy          write out the hierarchy as a flat .sim file

    argument            description

     <file>              .sim file to be written
     <design>            design to write

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_verilog

Write a Verilog representation of the specified design to a file.

Usage: nl_write_verilog [-hierarchy] [-libcell_stubs] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -hierarchy          recursively write out all linked subdesigns
    -libcell_stubs      write stub modules for libcell designs

    argument            description

     <file>              Verilog file to be written
     <design>            design to write

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_vim_def

Write out the design in VIM format.

Usage: nl_write_vim_def <file> [<design>]

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the VIM DEF file to write
     <design>            design to be written

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_vim_physcell

Write out the design in VIM format.

Usage: nl_write_vim_physcell <file> [<design>]

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the VIM file to write
     <design>            design to be written

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_vim_placement

Write out the placement information in VIM format.

Usage: nl_write_vim_placement [-cell_translate <string>] [-gridless] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -cell_translate <string>proc to call to translate cell names
    -gridless           write a VIM with a gridless scale

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the VIM file to write
     <design>            design to be written

************************************************************************

COMMAND: nl_write_vim_tech

Write out the design in VIM format.

Usage: nl_write_vim_tech [-clock_name <string>] [-cell_translate <string>] [-net_translate <string>] [-nohierarchy] [-port_translate <string>] <file> [<design>]

    option              description

    -clock_name <string>the name of the clock signal
    -cell_translate <string>proc to call to translate cell names
    -net_translate <string>proc to call to translate net names
    -nohierarchy        do not descend hierarchy
    -port_translate <string>proc to call to translate port names

    argument            description

     <file>              the name of the VIM file to write
     <design>            design to be written
